KHASI-ENGLISH DICTIONARY. A
A, the first letter in the Khasi Alphabet ; — int. oh ! ah !
*Abir, XI, n. red powder used in the Holi festival.
Ak ! int. ah ! ejaculation of disgust at an unpleasant smell.
Aku ! int. expressing disgust at a bad smell.
Akher-ka-sngi, ka, n. Domesday.
A-khia, u, n. an earnest man.
*Akor, ka, n. behaviour, conduct.
Ade, ad. may be, perhaps.
Adong, ka, n. prohibition; — v. to prohibit.
Ang, v. to open, to crack.
Ahor, ka, n. a marshy place, a swamp.
Ai, v. to give, to bestow.
Ai-bai-siew, v. to give money for buying things.
Aiu, ka, n. law, statute.
Ai-nishan, v. to name, to point out, to cite, identify.
Aiom, ka, n. season, time.
A-iu, p. what.
Ale, v. imper. come.
Alhia, a. lazy, idle.
Along, ka, n. a lock-up.
Am, v. to bite, to plant the teeth in.
Ap, v. to wait, to stay for.
Ar, a. two.
Arshah, ad. doubly, twice as much.
Arsut, adv. downwards.
*Asbab, ka, n. luggage.
At, v. to swell, to bulge out.
B. B, the second letter in the Khasi alphabet.
Ba, 1. conj. that, for, inasmuch as, since.
Babe, v. to rue, to repent.
Babha, a. good.
Bak-bak, ad. heedlessly.
Bakla, v. to err, to make a mistake.
Bad, conj. and ; — prep. with.
Baden, ka, n. an irrigated rice field.
Bang, a. tasty, savoury, palatable; — ka, n. a piece of bamboo.
Bahkhala, v. to be answerable for, to be responsible for.
'baibam, ka, n. allowance, diet expenses, stipend.
'baibat, ka, n. cash, ready-money.
'baikhrong, ka, n. toll, tax.
'bainong, ka, n. wages, salary.
'bai-seng, ka, n. capital, money for carrying on any business.
Balei ? ad. why ? for what reason.
Bam, v. to eat.
Bambriew, adj. cannibal, man-eating.
Bam-khuti, v. to take bribes.
Bam-krang, v. to undermine.
Bamram, v. to live in debt, to incur debt.
Bamsap, v. to take bribes; to commit secret faults.
Ban, v. to press upon, to treat cruelly, to oppress.
Banse, v. obliged to, to have no other alternative.
